newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 96/97 soybean harvest 60 pct sold - Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 96/97 soybean harvest 60 pct sold - Safras.

text.p: Brazilian farmers had sold 60 percent of the total expected 1996/97 soybean crop by the week ending April 24, independent consultants Safras e Mercado said.
This compared with 50 percent at the same stage in 1996 and an average of 48 percent over the last five years.
Forward sales were due to a combination of financing needs and prices, which were 10 to 15 percent higher on average than in 1996, Safras said in a weekly report.
The issue now was what to do with the remaining 40 percent of the forecast 26.2 million tonne crop, it added.
"Historically, the price in between harvests, expecially between November and January, is always better than during the harvest," it said.
"But in 1997, this could end up not happening, or if it does happen, it won't be in sufficient measure to justify holding stocks for such a long period," it added.

Hoarding stocks only made sense if one assumed a problem with the U.S. harvest, and the best advice to producers was to closely follow weather and planting news out of the U.S. and take advantage of any price peaks in May and August to sell.
